slides.title: Motivation: Aerodynamic Trade-offs in Modern Formula 1
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Overall vehicle aerodynamic efficiency L/D versus rear-wing angle.
bullet_points: Formula 1 aerodynamic development centers on the fundamental trade-off between downforce and induced drag.
Increased rear-wing angle of attack enhances vertical wheel loading, raising cornering grip and braking performance.
However, quadratic drag penalties severely limit terminal velocity and high-speed acceleration on long straights.
Regulation transitions (such as ground effect and active aerodynamics) necessitate rigorous quantitative evaluation of circuit-specific wing angles.

slides.title: Research Question and Project Objectives
bullet_points: Central Research Question: How does rear-wing incidence angle (0° to 30°) quantitatively govern vehicle downforce, induced drag, and lap time across diverse circuit archetypes?
Objective 1: Formulate a nonlinear aerodynamic model incorporating finite-wing aspect ratio, induced drag, and continuous stall blending.
Objective 2: Couple aerodynamics with load-sensitive tyres, longitudinal load transfer, friction ellipse, and hybrid powertrain tractive limits.
Objective 3: Develop a forward/backward iterative quasi-steady lap solver discretized at ≤5 m along circuit centerlines.
Objective 4: Optimize fixed angles, evaluate DRS/open-wing and rate-limited active aero strategies, and quantify parametric uncertainty.

slides.title: Aerodynamic Theory: Lift, Induced Drag, and Stall
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Wing lift and drag coefficients showing smooth hyperbolic tangent stall transition.
bullet_points: Finite-Wing Lift Correction: Wing lift curve slope corrected by aspect ratio AR = 3.8 and Oswald efficiency factor e = 0.88:
a_wing = a0 / (1 + a0 / (π · e · AR))
Induced Drag: Directly coupled to wing lift coefficient: CD,i = CL,wing² / (π · e · AR)
Stall Modeling: Continuous C¹-smooth tanh blending transitions lift from linear pre-stall to post-stall plateau at α_stall = 18.0°.
Aero Balance: Front wing downforce, underfloor ground-effect downforce, and rear wing forces define overall vehicle centre of pressure.

slides.title: Vehicle Dynamics: Tyre Load Sensitivity and G-G Ellipse
bullet_points: Tyre Load Sensitivity: Normal force de-rates tyre friction coefficient nonlinearly according to power-law decay:
μ(Fz) = μ_ref · (Fz / Fz,ref)^(-γ), with γ = 0.08, μ_ref = 1.80 at 3,000 N.
Friction Ellipse: Coupled traction and cornering limits prevent impossible simultaneous grip utilization:
(Fx / Fx,max)² + (Fy / Fy,max)² ≤ 1.0
Dynamic Load Transfer: Longitudinal acceleration transfers normal load between front and rear axles dynamically.
Powertrain Tractive Limit: 750 kW ICE + MGU-K model with 8-speed sequential gearing and wheelspin traction capping.

slides.title: System Architecture and Simulation Pipeline
bullet_points: Configuration Layer: Strict JSON schema validation ensuring physical consistency, immutable dataclasses, and SI unit enforcement.
Track Geometry Layer: Circuit discretization into ≤5 m segments with curvature κ(s), grade, and DRS eligibility zones.
Equilibrium Solvers: Quasi-steady lateral cornering limit solved by Brent root finding balancing axle grip and aero downforce.
Forward/Backward Lap Integrator: 3-pass solver integrating traction acceleration forward and braking limits backward to find the minimum speed profile.
Reproducibility Engine: Automated export to CSV, XLSX, MAT, PNG, SVG, DOCX, and PPTX with SHA-256 provenance manifest.

slides.title: Vehicle Parameters and Baseline Configuration
bullet_points: Representative Educational Parameters: Sourced from public Formula 1 technical regulations and academic literature.
Chassis: Total vehicle mass m = 798 kg, wheelbase L = 3.60 m, static front distribution = 45.5%, CG height = 0.31 m.
Baseline Aero: Front wing downforce = 6.2 kN at 250 km/h, underfloor = 11.5 kN, baseline vehicle drag CD,0 = 0.68.
Powertrain: Maximum power = 750 kW, 8 forward gear ratios from 3.15:1 to 0.92:1, final drive 4.10:1, drivetrain efficiency = 97.5%.
Tyres: Front width = 0.305 m, Rear width = 0.405 m, Rolling resistance Crr = 0.014.

slides.title: Aerodynamic Characterisation: Polar and Efficiency
slides.figure_caption: Figure: CL,total and CD,total polar showing drag penalty escalating sharply beyond stall.
bullet_points: Linear Wing Regime: From 0° to 12°, lift coefficient rises smoothly with slope ~0.075 deg⁻¹ as induced drag remains moderate.
Stall Region: Lift coefficient reaches peak at 18.0° (CL,total = 3.25), after which flow separation induces lift loss and drag growth.
Aero Efficiency Curve: Maximum vehicle aerodynamic efficiency (L/D ~ 3.42) occurs at 6.0°, far lower than maximum downforce.
Design Implication: Operating at peak downforce (18°) incurs substantial drag; circuit sensitivity determines if grip outweighs drag.

slides.title: Speed-Dependent Aerodynamic Forces and Balance
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Total vehicle downforce as a function of ground speed across representative wing angles.
bullet_points: Quadratic Force Scaling: Both downforce and drag scale with velocity squared (V²), dominating tyre load above 120 km/h.
High-Speed Loading: At 300 km/h (83.3 m/s), total downforce reaches 18.4 kN at 18° wing angle, exceeding twice the vehicle static weight.
Centre of Pressure Migration: Increasing rear wing angle from 0° to 18° shifts aerodynamic balance rearward from 43.8% to 37.2% front.
Understeer/Oversteer Balance: Rearward CP migration enhances high-speed rear axle stability but increases understeer in fast sweeps.

slides.title: Straight-Line Performance: Acceleration and Top Speed
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Maximum terminal velocity as a function of rear-wing angle showing 70 km/h loss across sweep.
bullet_points: Terminal Velocity Envelope: Equilibrium between engine wheel thrust and aero/rolling drag dictates top speed.
Top Speed Reduction: V_max drops monotonically from 348.6 km/h at 0° to 304.5 km/h at 18° and 278.4 km/h at 30°.
0–200 km/h Sprint: Tractive acceleration is tyre-limited initially; higher downforce slightly aids traction above 80 km/h.
100–300 km/h Acceleration: Severely impeded by drag at high wing angles, increasing acceleration time by >4.5 seconds.

slides.title: Cornering Performance and Lateral Limits
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Maximum lateral acceleration vs speed showing dramatic downforce benefits at high cornering velocity.
bullet_points: Low-Speed Cornering (50 km/h): Governed primarily by static mass and mechanical tyre grip (ay ~ 1.75g); wing angle effect < 4%.
Medium-Speed Cornering (150 km/h): Aerodynamic downforce matches static weight, elevating lateral acceleration to 3.1g at 18° vs 2.4g at 0°.
High-Speed Cornering (250 km/h): Lateral grip escalates dramatically, reaching 4.85g at 18° angle compared to 3.25g at 0°.
Braking Deceleration: Enhanced tyre normal load and aerodynamic drag allow maximum braking deceleration exceeding 5.2g from 300 km/h.

slides.title: Circuit Archetypes and Fixed-Angle Optimization
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Circuit lap times across 0°–30° sweep revealing contrasting low-, medium-, and high-downforce optima.
bullet_points: Low-Downforce Archetype (Monza style): Optimum fixed angle is 17.996° yielding minimum lap time of 68.150 s. Corner exits demand sufficient downforce to carry onto straight.
Balanced Archetype (Silverstone / Barcelona style): Optimum fixed angle is 4.997° yielding minimum lap time of 58.812 s. Moderate wing balances straight speed and high-speed corner grip.
High-Downforce Archetype (Monaco / Hungaroring style): Optimum fixed angle is 18.000° yielding minimum lap time of 64.528 s. Cornering traction heavily dominates drag penalty.
Post-Stall Penalty: Exceeding 18.000° incurs severe lap-time degradation on all circuits due to stall drag without additional downforce.

slides.title: Lap-Time Sweeps and Speed Traces
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Distance-domain velocity profiles comparing 0°, circuit optimum, and 25° over full lap.
bullet_points: Apex Velocity Gains: The optimum configuration yields +25 km/h in medium-speed corners and +42 km/h in high-speed sweeps over 0° trim.
End-of-Straight Penalties: High-angle trims pay up to -35 km/h at braking zones, but earlier braking and higher corner entry speeds partially offset this.
Throttle Duty Cycle: Full-throttle percentage drops from 74.2% at 18° to 63.8% at 0° due to traction limitations at corner exit.
Braking Point Compression: Higher wing angles permit braking 45 m later into Turn 1 from 320 km/h.

slides.title: Aerodynamic Strategies: Fixed, Open-Wing, and Active Aero
slides.figure_caption: Figure: Comparison of lap time benefits across Fixed, Open-Wing (DRS), and Actuator-Limited Active Aero.
bullet_points: Fixed-Angle Baseline: Compromised between cornering downforce and straight-line speed; cannot adapt dynamically.
Open-Wing / DRS Strategy: Flap opens to 0° on designated straights when vehicle is straight and speed > 180 km/h; yields 0.45 s to 1.15 s improvement.
Ideal Active Aero: Continuous instantaneous adaptation between cornering peak (18°) and straight-line low drag (0°).
Actuator-Limited Active Aero: Real-world 90°/s slew rate limit prevents instantaneous transitions; achieved lap times: Balanced 59.353 s, Low-DF 68.599 s, High-DF 64.615 s.

slides.title: Uncertainty Analysis and Global Parameter Sensitivity
slides.figure_caption: Figure: One-at-a-time ±10% sensitivity tornado diagram ranking input parameter impacts on lap time.
bullet_points: Monte Carlo Robustness: 1,000 evaluations per circuit (seed 3106) with Gaussian distributions for ambient density, tyre grip, engine power, and drag.
Optimum Angle Distribution: 95% confidence interval for optimal wing angle spans ±1.8° around nominal optima, demonstrating stability.
Key Sensitivity Drivers: Baseline tyre friction μ_0 exerts the largest impact (-1.42 s per +10%), followed by vehicle mass (+1.18 s) and engine power (-0.95 s).
Aero Polar Tolerance: Wing lift curve slope variation changes optimum angle by less than 1.2°, verifying robustness of recommended setup.

slides.title: Model Assumptions, Limitations, and Ethical Disclosure
bullet_points: Educational Model Classification: All parameters are representative educational values and do not reflect proprietary data from any Formula 1 team.
Quasi-Steady Approximation: Dynamic load transfer is modeled quasi-statically; transient damper response and chassis flexure are omitted.
Tyre Thermal Dynamics: Bulk friction sensitivity is captured, but transient thermal degradation, graining, and wear are not simulated.
Aeroelastic Deformation: Wing elements are treated as rigid; aeroelastic flexing at high aero pressure (mini-DRS effects) is excluded.
Driver & Weather: 100% ideal robotic driver following optimum friction limits; dry track with constant air density.

slides.title: Conclusions and Engineering Recommendations
bullet_points: Circuit-Specific Optimality: No single wing angle is universally optimal; balanced circuits favor moderate angles (5.00°), while high-downforce circuits demand stall-limit trim (18.00°).
Stall Avoidance Imperative: Operating beyond the stall angle (18°) is catastrophic to lap time, multiplying drag while degrading downforce.
Active Aero Control Lesson: Ideal active aero improves lap time by up to -0.54 s, but finite 90°/s slew rates and transition delays incur penalties (+0.09s to +0.54s) under naive threshold switching.
Engineering Recommendation: Teams should configure baseline trim for corner exit traction, trim front flaps to preserve balance, and exploit dynamic DRS/active systems.
Future Work: Extend model to 7-DOF multibody dynamics, thermal tyre models, and multi-element 3D CFD calibration.
